sentences.text: Revenue grew from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025, a 6.4% CAGR, in a cyclical rather than steady path [F1][F10][F201].
Revenue fell 22.4% in FY2020, which the filing attributes to lower sales volume from weaker end-user demand and dealer inventory changes [D198][P59].
Revenue rose 18.0% in FY2017, primarily on higher sales volume from improved end-user demand and favorable dealer inventory changes [D42][P68].
Operating income rose 64.0% in FY2023, mainly on price realization, volume and the absence of the $925 million Rail goodwill impairment of FY2022 [D358][P31][X117].
FY2025 revenue rose 4.3%, as higher sales volume was partly offset by unfavorable price realization of $817 million [D463][P13].
Power & Energy sales rose 11.6% to $32.2 billion, contributing 5.2pp of growth and reaching 47.6% of revenue [D758][S102][D759][D757].
Construction Industries sales fell 1.6% to $25.1 billion, as price realization cost $1.136 billion against volume gains of $568 million [D765][S105][P8].
Operating income fell 14.7% against revenue growth of 4.3%, with operating costs outgrowing revenue by 4.8pp [D464][D463][D489].
Diluted EPS fell 14.7%, less than the 17.7% drop in net income, because the diluted share count shrank 3.5% [D467][D465][D483].
Operating margin of 16.5% in FY2025 sits above the 14.3% window median but below the 20.2% high and well above the 3.0% low [F30][D1123][D1122][D1121].
Operating margin fell 3.7pp in FY2025, with cost of revenue taking 4.2pp, as manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion largely reflected higher tariffs [D476][D490][P9].
The largest move was FY2023, when operating margin rose 6.0pp, with cost of revenue adding 5.8pp; the filing cites favorable price realization and volume [D370][D384][P31].
Net margin of 13.1% trailed operating margin of 16.5%, with a 24.0% effective tax rate partly offset by $892 million of other income [F50][F30][D449][X110].
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion was 1.32x net income, while free cash flow of $8.9 billion matched net income at 1.00x [F80][D450][F100][D451].
Free cash flow to net income of 1.00x compares with a window median of 0.96x, and the 13.2% free cash flow margin with an 11.9% median [D451][D1135][D447][D1129].
Capital expenditures rose 41.9% to $2.82 billion, reaching 4.2% of revenue and 1.25x depreciation and amortization [D470][F90][D446][D452].
Free cash flow fell 11.2% mainly because capex rose faster than operating cash flow, which slipped 2.5% [D469][D470][D468].
Net cash (cash and investments less debt) was negative $26.2 billion, against negative $24.9 billion a year earlier [D456][D403].
Net cash was negative 38.8% of revenue, near the peer median of negative 35.6% and at the 43rd percentile of seven peers [D457][D1152][D1151].
Total debt rose 14.1% to $36.2 billion while cash rose 44.9% to $10.0 billion; the current ratio is 1.44x [D485][D455][D472][F140][F180].
Buybacks of $5.19 billion plus dividends of $2.75 billion took 89.0% of free cash flow, cutting the diluted share count 3.5% to 472.3 million [X140][X150][D459][D483][X130].
Net debt widened for a second straight year, to $26.2 billion from $24.9 billion, as debt grew 14.1% [R1][D403][D456][D485].
Operating income fell 14.7% and margin fell 3.7pp, driven by tariff-related manufacturing costs that management expects to persist into the first quarter of 2026 [D464][D476][P9][P14].
The FY2024 revenue decline of 3.4% looks benign, as FY2025 revenue of $67.6 billion exceeded FY2023's $67.1 billion [R2][D410][F10][F8].
Net income for FY2021 to FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy, so FY2025 shows $8,884 million against $8,882 million in the 10-K [R3][F40][X20].
Operating margin rising above FY2025's 16.5% would confirm easing tariff pressure, while a fall below the 14.3% window median would deepen it, in the FY2026 10-K [F30][D1123].

Construction Industries price realization turning positive, against the $1.136 billion drag in FY2025, would confirm the price-cost recovery management guides to for the first quarter of 2026, in the FY2026 10-K [P8][P15].
Free cash flow to net income falling below the 0.86x window low would show capex outrunning earnings, from the current 1.00x, in the FY2026 10-K [D1133][D451].
